passage:
The wedding reception held a small surprise: four exes under one roof. Hafsa saw hers laughing beside someone new, and jealousy stabbed her under the ribs. She did not open his profile to look. She stepped onto the balcony, remembered why she had left, thought of the pottery class she had booked, and rejoined the dance floor lighter.

Zubin stood by the buffet watching his ex chat easily. On the drive home he said to his girlfriend, "Priya's laugh was so effortless." Then he heard himself. He was setting a real person's ordinary Tuesday against the best clips of his memory. "Sorry," he said. "You make tea exactly how I like it. And I would love more time together at weekends." She smiled and said yes.

Eshaan still felt the burn of how his ex had spoken to him, and he told a friend so, quietly, in the corridor. He posted nothing and sent nothing. He booked a counsellor for the following week and went for a long walk.

At the far table sat Meher, who had parted from her ex years earlier. When he came over, she said, "I hope you are well. I stopped being angry a while ago." She wanted no apology and no reunion. She sat down again and finished her tea.

qa.q: Where did Eshaan tell a friend about his anger?
qa.a: He told a friend in the corridor.

qa.q: How did Eshaan's still-fresh anger differ from Meher's ease with her ex, and what did each do with it?
qa.a: Eshaan still felt the burn, so he confided in a friend and booked a counsellor without posting anything. Meher had let the resentment go years earlier and spoke briefly, asking for no apology and no reunion.

qa.q: What was Zubin feeling on the drive home, and what did he realise?
qa.a: He felt wistful and a little dissatisfied. Then he realised he was comparing his girlfriend's ordinary days with the best clips of his memory.

qa.q: What did Hafsa do instead of checking her ex's profile?
qa.a: She stepped onto the balcony, remembered why she had left, thought of her pottery class, and went back to the dance floor.

grounding: Four people at one wedding meet an ex with jealousy, comparison, lingering anger and settled forgiveness, each handled differently.
